statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail falls from 22 to 19 because the overnight break that drove the previous increase was rejected rather than extended. NQ probed a new session low at 30,651.25 and has since retraced 44 points to 30,695.50, quoted at 05:15 UTC, with no repeated extension and no failed retracement on record. The cross-asset stack still withholds confirmation: the 10-year is unchanged at 5.12%, the 2-year is slightly lower at 4.90%, and both crude benchmarks are down. Stress eases only two points to 50 because the elevated-yield environment behind Wednesday's decline is unresolved.
recommendation: Tail is back in the low band and the mapped policy state returns to EA_ON. The published danger window is unchanged at the 24 September U.S. cash open, 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, where opening-auction continuation is the structure that would deny retracement. The 12:30 UTC jobless-claims block and the 17:00 UTC seven-year note auction are the secondary checkpoints, the latter carrying extra weight after Wednesday's poorly received sale. A sustained loss of 30,651.25 would reopen the downside probe and argue for a higher state; a reclaim of 30,704.50 with the 10-year holding at or below 5.12% would confirm the rejection is complete. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reject the 30,651.25 session low and retrace 44 points, with a flat 5.12% 10-year still withholding the rates confirmation
body:
The live Globex path is the decisive evidence and it has resolved in favour of mean reversion. Nasdaq-100 December futures trade 30,695.50, down 69.25 points or 0.23%, quoted at 05:15 UTC against a 30,780.00 open and a 30,764.75 prior close. The session low of 30,651.25 was printed and then rejected: price now sits 44.25 points above it, roughly 27% of the way back up a 161.75-point overnight range. That is precisely the retracement whose absence the previous assessment was measuring, and it is why Tail returns from 22 to 19 and the mapped state from WATCH to EA_ON.

The confirmation named an hour ago has not occurred. Sustained trade below 30,651.75 was the condition for a worse path; instead the low held within half a point of that level and reversed. The reclaim of 30,704.50 that would complete the invalidation is nine points away and not yet achieved, which is the one reason Tail sits at the top of the low band rather than deeper inside it. What matters for the price-path measure is that only a single downside leg has been observed across the whole session, there is no sequence of shallow pullbacks, and no retracement has failed.

The cross-asset stack continues to withhold confirmation, and that is the more important structural point. The 10-year Treasury yield is quoted 5.12% for 24 September, effectively unchanged on the day, with the 2-year at 4.90% marginally lower, the 5-year at 5.01% and the 30-year at 5.41%. Wednesday's move was violent by comparison: the 10-year surged roughly 16 basis points to its highest level since July 2007 after the S&P Global flash composite PMI printed 58.4, the strongest in over five years, and a poorly received auction added to the pressure. Fed funds futures moved to price a large majority probability of an October hike and Governor Barr said further increases would likely be needed. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.13% to 26,936.04, the S&P 500 0.75% and the Dow 0.68%. None of that impulse is extending now. Both crude benchmarks are lower, WTI at $91.57 and Brent at $102.36, each down around 0.7% amid uncertainty over US-Iran negotiations and a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which relieves rather than reinforces the inflation channel. The VIX closed at 15.18, up 6.83% on Wednesday but still an absolute level that prices no sustained dislocation. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,755.00, down 0.23% with the session low unchanged at 7,742.25, have bounced in step, confirming the rebound is index-wide rather than a Nasdaq-specific impulse.

Supporting context remains thin. The shared Finviz collection is partial and its latest payload is roughly three and three-quarter hours old, well past the 90-minute freshness limit, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable. Its latest-session breadth is therefore used only as background: semiconductors were negative across all seven names tracked with a mean of -1.36%, and only three of eight megacaps closed higher, led lower by Alphabet at -3.80% and Broadcom at -2.62%. That is delayed, non-real-time colour describing Wednesday rather than evidence of the current price path, and it informs Stress rather than Tail.

The day ahead keeps one dense catalyst cluster. Initial and continuing jobless claims print at 12:30 UTC alongside the Q2 current account, the U.S. cash open follows at 13:30 UTC, New Home Sales arrive at 14:00 UTC and a seven-year note auction settles at 17:00 UTC, with Williams, Barkin, Hammack and Paulson all scheduled. The published danger window is unchanged at 13:30 to 15:00 UTC because the opening auction remains the one place where a fresh directional leg could become the persistent one-way path that Tail measures. Given Wednesday's weak auction, the 17:00 UTC seven-year sale is the session's most specific secondary checkpoint. The invalidation for the published low-Tail path is a sustained loss of 30,651.25; the confirmation that the rejection is complete is a reclaim of 30,704.50 with the 10-year holding at or below its current 5.12%.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Tail ran between 10 and 12 through the Asian and European hours of 23 September with Stress in the low-to-mid 30s, then stepped sharply to 25 with Stress 54 at 14:00 UTC as the U.S. cash open met a surge in the 10-year yield after hot flash PMIs; that remains the single hour in the window mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail then held a 20 to 24 plateau across the U.S. afternoon and into the overnight session before easing to 18, 17 and 18 in the 01:00 to 03:00 UTC hours, and rose again to 22 at 04:00 UTC on the break of the overnight low. Those are the opinions published at the time and are not restated with hindsight.
outlookSummary: The published path assumes the rejected session low holds, so the mapped state stays at EA_ON with Tail between 18 and 19 through the Asian and European hours. Conditional risk then builds into the U.S. session: Tail steps to 21 through the 12:30 UTC claims block and peaks at 23 across the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours that contain the cash open and the published danger window, the interval where an opening auction could convert a fresh leg into a persistent one-way path. Scores then decay across the afternoon, the seven-year auction and the 20:00 UTC cash close, returning to the low band from 20:00 UTC onward and easing to a published low of 16 in the quiet Friday Asian hours. No slot in the path reaches the block threshold. Every score beyond the current hour is conditional risk rather than observed structure, and confidence falls with forecast distance.
